055. Map it to the Pandas submissionQuestion: how does Pandas replace manual user lookup and daily counting? A DataFrame is a table with named columns. Keep the first four sample trips: build a table of allowed user IDs, keep trips matching at both endpoints, then collect rows sharing a day. The following are fixed worked values, independent of the trace position above.Build active: users["banned"] == "No" produces true/false for each user; .loc[condition, ["users_id"]] keeps the true rows and just the users_id column. Only user 2 of the eight users is banned, so active is a one-column table: users_id = [1, 3, 4, 10, 11, 12, 13].First merge: rename changes active’s column name to client_id, keeping the ID values. merge(..., on="client_id") pairs rows with equal client_id; its default inner behavior keeps only matched rows. #1’s 1 matches 1; #2’s 2 has no match; #3’s 3 and #4’s 4 match. The intermediate table contains #1, #3, #4, still carrying their driver_id, status and request_at.Second merge: rename active’s column to driver_id and match the intermediate rows by driver. #1→10, #3→12 and #4→13 all match, leaving #1, #3, #4. If driver 13 were banned, active would lack 13: #4 would pass the client check but disappear in the second merge. Unique users_id values ensure a match never multiplies one trip; distinct trips with identical payloads still count separately.Build window: between("2013-10-01", "2013-10-03") keeps dates including both endpoints; .copy() creates a working table so adding a column does not alter the input. All three rows are on 10-01. status.ne("completed") tests for inequality, giving [False, False, True]; .astype(int) converts these into the cancelled column [0, 0, 1]. The official three-status enum guarantees that non-completed means cancelled.Group and aggregate: groupby("request_at", as_index=False)["cancelled"] collects cancelled values with the same date, keeping the date as an ordinary column. The 10-01 group is [0, 0, 1]. .agg(["sum", "count"]) adds the values and counts them: sum = 1, count = 3. rename calls these cancelled and requests; dividing and round(2) gives 0.33. Finally rename request_at to Day and return only Day and Cancellation Rate. A day with no eligible rows has no group, so no 0/0 is produced.Cost: T = Trips rows, U = Users rows. Filter Users once to build active, then two merges use hash tables (ID-based lookup tables) to find matches without scanning U users per trip; hash lookup takes constant time on average. Next filter dates, build cancelled and group by day. Each stage takes expected O(T + U) time; even if grouping sorts keys, at most three dates remain. Total expected time is O(T + U). Lookup tables, intermediate merge tables and working columns require O(T + U) extra space. This is submission cost, separate from the teaching trace’s storage.One more transfer: client 7 and driver 70 are unbanned; driver 71 is banned. On 10-01, 7→70 has a completed and a cancelled_by_client trip; 10-02 has only a cancelled_by_driver trip 7→71; there is also a cancellation on 09-30. The two merges keep the driver-70 trips; the date filter then excludes 09-30. The 10-01 group is [0, 1], giving 0.50; 10-02 has no group and no output. Client-only filtering would incorrectly emit 10-02 at 1.00.Official Python/Pandas sourceCopy sourceDownload solution.pyClipboard access was denied; copy from the text area below.Official Python/Pandas sourceimport pandas as pd


def trips_and_users(trips: pd.DataFrame, users: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return daily cancellation rates for trips with two unbanned endpoints."""
    active = users.loc[users["banned"] == "No", ["users_id"]]
    eligible = trips.merge(active.rename(columns={"users_id": "client_id"}), on="client_id")
    eligible = eligible.merge(active.rename(columns={"users_id": "driver_id"}), on="driver_id")
    window = eligible.loc[
        eligible["request_at"].between("2013-10-01", "2013-10-03")
    ].copy()
    window["cancelled"] = window["status"].ne("completed").astype(int)
    result = (
        window.groupby("request_at", as_index=False)["cancelled"]
        .agg(["sum", "count"])
        .rename(columns={"sum": "cancelled", "count": "requests"})
    )
    result["Cancellation Rate"] = (result["cancelled"] / result["requests"]).round(2)
    return result.rename(columns={"request_at": "Day"})[["Day", "Cancellation Rate"]]
The executable submission interface is `trips_and_users(trips: pd.DataFrame, users: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame`. The code below is an offline mirror of that interface; the animation is only a teaching simulation.Related conceptsSee index placement in #41 (a different algorithm) →See neighbor-constraint scans in #135 (a different algorithm) →

033. Derive the invariantQuestion: why are the counts still correct after the next row? An invariant is a fact that stays true after each step; a prefix means the rows processed so far, starting at the beginning. For each day, (numerator, denominator) counts eligible cancellations and requests in that prefix. Initially both are (0, 0). An out-of-window or banned-endpoint excluded row changes neither count; an eligible completed row adds 1 only to denominator; an eligible cancelled row adds 1 to both. Each step adds exactly the new row’s contribution, preserving the fact. After all rows, the counts cover the whole window.A correct baseline loops over every trip for each of the three days. For each trip on that day, scan all Users once for its client’s ban flag and again for its driver’s flag, then count. Let T be the number of Trips rows and U the number of Users rows. Using just the first four sample trips and all eight users: three days require 3 × 4 = 12 trip-date checks; four matching trips each make two full eight-row user scans, totaling 4 × 2 × 8 = 64 user-row checks. In general this is at most 3T date checks plus 2TU user-row checks: O(T + TU) time and O(1) extra space for at most three daily counters, excluding inputs. Three days is a fixed constant; the avoidable growing cost is searching the same users again for every trip.Check the sample: after completed #1 the pair is (0, 1). Although #2 is cancelled, client 2 is banned, so it stays (0, 1), rather than (1, 2). Completed #3 makes (0, 2); eligible cancelled #4 makes (1, 3). Rewind and replay #2: neither count should change.excluded row → both counts unchanged
eligible row → denominator += 1
eligible cancelled row → numerator += 1
for days with eligible requests: rate = numerator / denominator

055. 映射到 Pandas 提交这一步要回答：Pandas 怎样代替手动找用户和逐日计数？DataFrame 是带列名的表。沿用示例前四条行程，先构造可匹配的用户 ID 表，再保留两端都匹配的行，最后把同一天的行收进一组。以下是固定的手算中间值，不随上方追踪位置改变。构造 active：users["banned"] == "No" 为每个用户产生真/假；.loc[条件, ["users_id"]] 只取条件为真的行和 users_id 列。八条 Users 中只有 2 被封，所以 active 是单列表 users_id = [1, 3, 4, 10, 11, 12, 13]。第一次 merge：rename 把 active 的列名改成 client_id（ID 值不变）。merge(..., on="client_id") 按相等的 client_id 配对行，默认 inner 表示只保留有匹配的行。#1 的 1 匹配 1，#2 的 2 没有匹配，#3 的 3 和 #4 的 4 都能匹配。中间表留下 #1, #3, #4，仍带着各自的 driver_id、status、request_at。第二次 merge：再把 active 的列名改成 driver_id，按司机匹配中间表。#1→10、#3→12、#4→13 都匹配，因此结果仍是 #1, #3, #4。若把司机 13 封禁，active 不再有 13：#4 会通过客户检查，却在第二次 merge 被排除。Users 的 users_id 唯一，所以一次匹配不会复制一条 trip；不同 trip 即使内容相同也分别计数。构造 window：between("2013-10-01", "2013-10-03") 保留含首尾的日期，.copy() 创建工作表，避免给输入添加列。三条都在 10-01。status.ne("completed") 判断不等于 completed，得到 [False, False, True]；.astype(int) 将其转成 cancelled 列 [0, 0, 1]。官方三种状态保证不等于 completed 就是取消。分组与汇总：groupby("request_at", as_index=False)["cancelled"] 把日期相同的 cancelled 值放在一起，并将日期保留为普通列。10-01 这一组是 [0, 0, 1]。.agg(["sum", "count"]) 对每组求和并数值的个数：sum = 1，count = 3。rename 把它们命名为 cancelled 和 requests；相除并 round(2) 得 0.33。最后把 request_at 改名 Day，只返回 Day 与 Cancellation Rate 两列。没有合资格行的日期没有组，所以不会产生 0/0。成本：T = Trips 行数，U = Users 行数。一次筛选 Users 建立 active，随后两次 merge 用按 ID 查找的哈希表（由 ID 快速定位匹配行），避免每条 trip 都扫描 U 行；哈希查找平均为常数时间。再筛日期、建 cancelled 列和按日期分组。每阶段期望 O(T + U) 时间；即使分组排序，日期最多三组。因此总期望 O(T + U) 时间。哈希表、两次连接的中间表和工作列最多占 O(T + U) 额外空间。这是提交成本，不是上方教学追踪的存储成本。再迁移一次：客户 7、司机 70 未封，司机 71 被封。10-01 有 7→70 的 completed 与 cancelled_by_client；10-02 只有 7→71 的 cancelled_by_driver；另有一条 09-30 的取消。两次 merge 后保留司机 70 的行，日期筛选再排除 09-30。10-01 组为 [0, 1]，输出 0.50；10-02 没有组，不输出。只查客户会错误地给 10-02 输出 1.00。官方 Python/Pandas 源码复制源码下载 solution.py浏览器拒绝剪贴板；请从下方文本框复制。官方 Python/Pandas 源码import pandas as pd


def trips_and_users(trips: pd.DataFrame, users: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return daily cancellation rates for trips with two unbanned endpoints."""
    active = users.loc[users["banned"] == "No", ["users_id"]]
    eligible = trips.merge(active.rename(columns={"users_id": "client_id"}), on="client_id")
    eligible = eligible.merge(active.rename(columns={"users_id": "driver_id"}), on="driver_id")
    window = eligible.loc[
        eligible["request_at"].between("2013-10-01", "2013-10-03")
    ].copy()
    window["cancelled"] = window["status"].ne("completed").astype(int)
    result = (
        window.groupby("request_at", as_index=False)["cancelled"]
        .agg(["sum", "count"])
        .rename(columns={"sum": "cancelled", "count": "requests"})
    )
    result["Cancellation Rate"] = (result["cancelled"] / result["requests"]).round(2)
    return result.rename(columns={"request_at": "Day"})[["Day", "Cancellation Rate"]]
可执行提交接口是 `trips_and_users(trips: pd.DataFrame, users: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame`。下方代码展示的是官方接口的离线镜像；动画只是教学模拟。相关概念去 #41 看原地索引放置（另一种算法） →去 #135 看相邻约束扫描（另一种算法） →

033. 从观察得到不变量这一步要回答：为什么处理下一行后，计数仍然正确？不变量是每一步都成立的事实；前缀就是从开头到当前已处理的这些行。对每个日期，(numerator, denominator) 分别是前缀内合资格的取消数与请求数。初始都是 (0, 0)。窗口外或任一端被封的排除行不改变任何计数；合资格且 completed 的行只给 denominator 加 1；合资格且取消的行给两个计数各加 1。每一步只计入新行应有的贡献，所以事实继续成立。处理完所有行，就得到整个窗口的计数。正确基线：对窗口内的每一天，循环检查所有 trip 的日期；对当天每条 trip，完整扫描 Users 一次找客户、再完整扫描一次找司机的 banned 标志，然后才计数。令 T 为 Trips 行数、U 为 Users 行数。只取示例的前四条 trip 和全部八条 Users：三天检查 3 × 4 = 12 次 trip 日期；四条当天请求各做两遍八行扫描，共 4 × 2 × 8 = 64 次用户行检查。一般至多 3T 次日期检查和 2TU 次用户行检查，时间 O(T + TU)、额外空间 O(1)（最多三天的计数，不含输入）。三天是固定常数；真正可避免的增长是每条 trip 都重新寻找同一批用户。对照示例：#1 completed 后是 (0, 1)。#2 虽然取消，但客户 2 被封，因此仍是 (0, 1)，不是 (1, 2)。#3 completed 后变成 (0, 2)，#4 合资格且取消后变成 (1, 3)。点上一行再重放 #2，两个计数都应不变。排除行 → 两个计数不变
合资格行 → denominator += 1
合资格且取消的行 → numerator += 1
有合资格请求的日期：rate = numerator / denominator
